correctness.rationale: If g=L_fv is nonzero somewhere on a closed orbit, continuity gives a uniformly bounded forward exit for nearby initial points, ruling out reachability; otherwise g=0 on orbit. A small Poincare map P has Q=P^2 increasing even on a nonorientable 2D manifold; for a transverse u, either Q(u)<=u gives perpetual forward confinement or Q(u)>=u gives backward confinement, including intermediate returns and all sufficiently nearby points. Since |g|<s on a tubular neighborhood, at least one exit time is infinite, which contradicts the two-finite-exit definition. In 3D q=x²+y² obeys qdot=2q(q-1)/(q+1), z(t)=eps exp(-t), angular speed 1. On q=1,z=0 the transverse exponents are +1,-1; for q(0)=1+eps,z(0)=eps the monotone g=2q(q-1)/(q+1)-z ranges from -infinity to +infinity. The first integral (q-1)^2/q=eps² exp(2t)/(1+eps) gives forward exit log(1/eps)+log((q_s-1)/sqrt(q_s))+o(1), backward log(1/eps)+log s+o(1), with q_s solving 2q_s(q_s-1)/(q_s+1)=s. Independent algebraic/numerical checks corroborate; the 2D topological argument supplies unrestricted exclusion.
